entities.name: Muhammad ibn Shakir al-Kutubi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abū ʿAbdallāh Muḥammad ibn Shākir al-Dārānī al-Dimashqī al-Kutubī (1287–1363) stands as a pivotal Mamluk-era historian and merchant, whose monumental biographical dictionary, *Fawāt al-Wafayāt* (The Departed of the Obituaries), offers an indispensable window into the intellectual and social fabric of 13th and 14th-century Syria and Egypt. Born in Damascus, al-Kutubi’s dual identity as a bookseller (al-Kutubī) and a scholar provided him with unparalleled access to contemporary literary circles and historical sources, enabling him to meticulously document the lives of hundreds of notable figures from the Ayyubid and Mamluk periods.

Al-Kutubi's primary contribution, *Fawāt al-Wafayāt*, was conceived as a supplement to the celebrated *Wafayāt al-Aʿyān* (Obituaries of Eminent Men) by Ibn Khallikan (d. 1282). While Ibn Khallikan focused on figures who died before 1256 CE, al-Kutubi systematically extended this tradition, compiling biographies of individuals who passed away between 1256 and his own time, up to 1358 CE. His work encompasses a diverse array of personalities, including rulers, scholars, poets, jurists, Sufis, and administrators, often providing unique details not found in other contemporary chronicles. His methodical approach and attention to detail make it a critical resource for understanding the cultural and political landscape of the Mamluk Sultanate, particularly during the Bahri Mamluk period.
